slides.say: Now a new question. A B C D is a trapezoid with A B parallel to D C. Its diagonals meet at O. Given, A B is four and D C is six. The area of triangle A O B is eight. What is the area of the trapezoid?
So we know one small triangle, and we need the whole trapezoid. The diagonals cut the trapezoid into four triangles.
Look at the top triangle, A O B, and the bottom one, C O D. A B is parallel to D C, so this is an hourglass, like in the lesson.
So the two triangles are similar. A B matches D C, because both are opposite the vertical angles at O. Four to six is two to three.
at: Four to six is two to three

slides.say: The area ratio is the square. Two squared is four, and three squared is nine. So the top triangle is four units, and the bottom one is nine units.
at: So the top triangle is four

slides.say: Now the triangles on the sides. Look at A O D and A O B. They're not similar. But they have the same height, from A down to the diagonal B D.
at: Now the triangles on the sides

slides.say: So their areas follow their bases on B D. The bases are O B and O D.
at: The bases are O B and O D

slides.say: O B is in the top triangle, and O D is in the bottom one. In the hourglass, they're matching sides. So O B to O D is two to three, like A B to D C.
at: So O B to O D

slides.say: So A O B to A O D is two to three as well. A O B is four units, and four is two times two. So A O D is three times two, six units.
at: So A O B to A O D

slides.say: The other side triangle, B O C, works the same way, from C. It's also six units.
In all, four plus six plus six plus nine is twenty-five units.
The top triangle is four units, and its area is eight. So one unit is eight divided by four, two.
at: The top triangle is four units

slides.say: The trapezoid is twenty-five units. Twenty-five times two is fifty.
Careful with twenty-six. That's only the top and the bottom, four plus nine units, times two. It forgets the side triangles.
And forty-two treats each side triangle as four units, like the top one.
Here's one fact worth remembering. When the bases are a and b, the four triangles are always a squared, a times b, a times b, and b squared. Here that's four, six, six and nine.
Choice number three is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
